Lab briefing

Study the core ideas before starting the practical work.

+Add−Subtract×* Multiply÷/ Divide//Whole division%Remainder**Power

Order of operations

total = 4 + 3 * 2       # 10
total = (4 + 3) * 2     # 14

Brackets are processed first, followed by powers, multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.

Readable output

cost = 12.5
print(f"Total: £{cost:.2f}")

An f-string places values inside text. :.2f displays a number to two decimal places without changing the stored value.

Grouping

fullTeams = players // teamSize
leftOver = players % teamSize

// finds complete groups. % finds the remainder.

Percentages and discounts

discount = price * 0.20
salePrice = price - discount

Calculate the amount to remove, then subtract it from the original price. Store stages separately so they are easy to test.

A running program can still be wrong

Estimate first, then test with values whose answer you already know. Use round(value, 2) only when the rounded value must be stored.

    PYTHON LAB REFERENCE
    Support & examples
    Use this page as an operator and formatting reference. None of the examples duplicate a build solution.
    Key concepts
    • Python follows operator precedence; brackets make an intended order clear.
    • / gives ordinary division, // gives whole groups and % gives the remainder.
    • Use ** for powers, such as side ** 2.
    • Use f-strings to combine labels, variables and calculations.
    • Format money to two decimal places with :.2f.
    Common errors
    • Using + where multiplication is required
    • Using / when whole groups and a remainder are needed
    • Forgetting brackets in a multi-step formula
    • Displaying unformatted money such as £7.5
    Misconceptions to avoid
    Misconception: rounding fixes an inaccurate formula
    Rounding only changes precision. The calculation must still be correct.
    Misconception: // and % do the same job
    // gives the number of complete groups; % gives what remains.
    Misconception: An f-string changes the stored value
    Formatting affects the displayed text, not the original numerical variable.
    EXAMPLE 01 · SCALING A VALUE
    Recipe batch calculator
    servings = int(input("Required servings: "))
flourPerServing = 45
totalFlour = servings * flourPerServing
print(f"Flour required: {totalFlour} g")
    The calculation combines a user value with a fixed amount.
    EXAMPLE 02 · WHOLE GROUPS AND REMAINDER
    Coach timetable
    totalMinutes = int(input("Training time in minutes: "))
hours = totalMinutes // 60
minutes = totalMinutes % 60
print(f"Training time: {hours} h {minutes} min")
    Integer division finds complete hours and remainder finds the minutes left over.
    EXAMPLE 03 · DECIMAL FORMATTING
    Fuel estimate
    litres = float(input("Litres required: "))
pricePerLitre = 1.47
cost = litres * pricePerLitre
print(f"Estimated fuel cost: £{cost:.2f}")
    The stored value remains precise; only the displayed value is formatted.
